decisions.difference: A: known-diabetes check triggered by glucose < 4 only (known diabetes asked inside the high-glucose task)  vs  B: known-diabetes task triggered by (or (< glucose 4) (>= glucose 11.1))
decisions.final_expr: (or (< (measurement (snomed_concept "Blood glucose status" "observable entity") mmol/L) 4) (>= (measurement (snomed_concept "Blood glucose status" "observable entity") mmol/L) 11.1))
decisions.reason: The page needs to know about diabetes on both the low branch ("< 4 if diabetes") and the high branch ("No ketones • If known diabetes …"); B asks for it once on both, A asks for it on both too but via two tasks.

decisions.difference: A: one task for all glucose >= 11.1 checks  vs  B: separate tasks for red box 2 signs, urine ketones (>= 11.1), and diabetes symptoms (>= 11.1, (no Ketonuria), (no known diabetes))
decisions.final_expr: (and (>= glucose 11.1) (no (clinical_finding Ketonuria)) (no (clinical_finding Diabetes mellitus + Known present)))
decisions.reason: The page asks the symptoms question only after "No ketones" and "If not known diabetes"; B's staged triggers follow that sequence, and its due_to also checks for the (no known diabetes) evidence, so A's known checker issue disappears.

decisions.difference: A: Acute confusion  vs  B: Clouded consciousness (also in priority rule)
decisions.reason: The page says plain "Confusion"; Clouded consciousness is SNOMED's concept carrying the synonym Confusion and Acute confusion is its descendant, so the general concept matches the page's general word.

decisions.difference: A: Signs of dehydration (finding)  vs  B: Dehydration (disorder) (also in priority rule)
decisions.reason: The page writes "Dehydration⁷" and does not say whether the recorded form is the disorder or its footnote-7 signs; Dehydration is the page's literal word.

decisions.difference: A: known diabetes in the high-glucose task's check_for  vs  B: known diabetes in the shared known-diabetes task
decisions.reason: Same finding, checked once by the task whose trigger covers both glucose branches that ask "known diabetes".

decisions.difference: A: Urgent hypoglycaemia = (or (< glucose 3) (and (< glucose 4) known diabetes))  vs  B: (active_condition Hypoglycemia)
decisions.reason: The page names the diagnosis ("Patient has hypoglycaemia") and then "Give urgent attention", and Will's briefing says to reference the probable diagnosis via active_condition; A's concern that it may match a past hypoglycaemia goes to the clinician.

decisions.difference: A: one Urgent rule for glucose >= 11.1 with (or red box 2 items … Ketonuria)  vs  B: two Urgent rules, red box 2 signs and ketones separately
decisions.final_expr: (and (>= glucose 11.1) (clinical_finding Ketonuria)) as its own rule
decisions.reason: The page reaches red box 3 by two separate arrows ("Yes" from red box 2 and "Ketones present"); B's two rules mirror them, and the logic equals A's.

notes: Both builds passed. The final build is builder B's encoding unchanged in the .lisp. The two builds agreed on everything else, including both diagnosis rules. Both left out the fasting glucose branch (no fasting-glucose observable), the type 1 rule for under-35s (no age criterion) and the requirement that every red-box-2 item is 'No' before the ketone check. Builder A's clinician questions are merged in: Emergency for glucose < 3, active_condition matching past hypoglycaemia, footnote-7 dehydration signs, and whether 'No ketones' is enough. Two reconciler judgment calls were added to provenance.
